SECTION I: EXPLOSIVE HAZARDS, UNEXPLODED ORDNANCE (UXO) & ZERO TOUCH RULE

1.1. Core Conflict Zone Postulate
In active combat theaters, post-conflict areas, and contested gray zones, one inviolable law governs survival:
EVERY OBJECT LOCATED ON THE GROUND, BURIED, OR IN ABANDONED STRUCTURES MUST BE REGARDED AS LETHAL AND BOOBY-TRAPPED UNTIL OFFICIALLY CLEARED BY PROFESSIONAL HUMANITARIAN DEMINERS.

The Zero Touch Rule:
- Strictly forbidden: touching, picking up, kicking, moving, covering, or attempting to dismantle any encountered object.
- No curiosity, material worth (currency, jewelry, high-end electronics), or utilitarian value (abandoned firearms, ammo cans, tools) justifies the risk of instant death or traumatic limb amputation.

1.2. Taxonomy of Booby Traps and Disguised IEDs
A booby trap is an explosive device disguised as an innocuous everyday object, rigged to detonate upon natural human interaction (lifting, opening a lid, pressing a switch).

Categories of Trapped Items:
1. Consumer Electronics:
   - Smartphones, tablets, power banks, handheld radios, flashlights, USB drives.
   - Mechanism: The lithium battery is hollowed out and replaced with 50-200 grams of military plastic explosive (C-4, Semtex, RDX) and an electric initiator wired to the power switch or tilt sensor. Detonates in hands, obliterating fingers, facial bones, and eyesight.
2. Attractive Domestic Items:
   - Cigarette packs, lighters, thermoses, beverage cans, wristwatches, wallets, bags.
   - Children's toys: dolls, teddy bears, remote control cars, bright balls. Deliberately engineered to entice children.
3. Abandoned Military Equipment:
   - Rifles, pistols, RPG tubes, ammunition crates, helmets, plate carriers, IFAK kits.
   - Pressure-release traps (e.g. ML-7 / MS-3): Placed beneath rifle buttstocks or ammo crates. The firing pin is held back by the weight of the item; lifting the rifle by even 3 millimeters triggers an instantaneous blast.
4. Human Casualties and Dead Livestock:
   - Rigged with tripwires or pressure-release devices beneath bodies. Approach must be conducted solely by sappers using standoff grapnel hooks (50+ meters) from heavy cover.
5. Abandoned Vehicles:
   - Doors, pedals, gas caps, glove boxes, and trunks wired to electrical switches.

1.3. Tripwires and Subtle Obstacles
A tripwire is a mechanical trip-line connecting a target to an explosive fuse (e.g. grenade pin, POM-2, OZM-72 bounding mine).
- Composition: Ultra-thin dark nylon line, braided steel wire, or fine copper thread (0.1-0.2 mm).
- Installation heights: Ankle height (10-15 cm), knee height (40-50 cm), or chest height (100-150 cm in doorframes and dense brush).
- Action if you snag a tripwire: FREEZE INSTANTLY. Do not jerk back. Shout: "HALT! GRENADE! DOWN!". If a grenade striker clicked, you have 3 to 4 seconds: dive away, feet toward blast, hands covering ears, mouth open.

1.4. Scatterable Butterfly Mines (PFM-1) and Cluster Munitions
- PFM-1 'Butterfly' Mines: Weight 80g, 12cm long. Soft polyethylene wing molded in green or khaki. Filled with liquid explosive VS-6D. Hydraulic pressure trigger fires under 5-25 kg (a child's footstep). The PFM-1S variant incorporates an unpredictable self-destruct timer (1 to 40 hours) detonating spontaneously without physical touch.
- Cluster Submunitions: Dispersed by Grad, Uragan, Smerch, HIMARS. Cylindrical bomblets with nylon ribbon stabilizers. 20-30% failure-to-explode rate; fuses remain armed on ground or in tree canopies, hair-trigger sensitive to footsteps or sunlight heating.

1.5. Anti-Tank Mines (TM-62M)
- Blast charge: 7.5 to 8 kg of TNT.
- Secondary anti-handling traps: Often installed with bottom or side booby-trap fuses (MUV, MS-3). Attempting to lift or disarm an anti-tank mine manually causes total obliteration.
- Civilian vehicle risk: Passenger vehicles (1.2-2.0 tons) easily exceed the fuse threshold. Never drive on unpaved shoulders or grassy detours; stay strictly on compacted heavy-vehicle tracks.

================================================================================

SECTION II: COUNTER-UAV SURVIVAL & DRONE EVASION TACTICS

2.1. Aerial Threat Profiles
1. Strike FPV Kamikaze Drones:
   - High-speed racing quads (7-10 inch) piloted via FPV goggles. Terminal dive velocity: 100-160 km/h. Carries RPG-7 shaped charges (PG-7V), thermobaric munitions, or anti-personnel fragmentation blocks.
2. Dropper Drones (Mavic 3, Matrice 300, Heavy Hexacopters):
   - Hover at 50-300 meters, dropping grenades with optical crosshairs. Equipped with high-resolution thermal sensors.
3. Fixed-Wing Reconnaissance UAVs (Orlan, ZALA, Supercam, Puma):
   - Loiter at 1000-3000 meters for hours, spotting targets for artillery and guiding FPV attack waves.

2.2. Audio Signatures and Time Window
- Piercing, high-RPM screaming turbine whine (20,000+ RPM).
- Dive phase: 2 to 3 seconds from acoustic crescendo to impact. Immediate protective reaction required.

2.3. Critical Errors During Drone Attack
1. Never sprint in a straight line down open roads or fields. Humans run at 15-20 km/h; drones dive at 140 km/h.
2. Never seek cover inside civilian vehicles. Shaped-charge warheads slice through auto sheet metal effortlessly.
3. Do not attempt handgun fire against a diving 140 km/h drone.

2.4. Lateral 90-Degree Evasion Maneuver
1. Listen constantly: Uncover ears, forbid headphones, keep vehicle windows cracked.
2. Determine vector: Locate inbound sky sector.
3. Exploit drone inertia: At 130 km/h, the drone has massive forward momentum. The fixed-camera pilot cannot abruptly redirect lateral flight without losing orientation.
4. Violent 90-degree lateral sprint: 1-2 seconds prior to impact, sprint perpendicular to the drone's flight vector behind a massive barrier (40cm+ oak tree, concrete abutment, brick building corner, culvert).
5. Prone position: Dive feet toward blast, elbows tucked, hands over neck/ears, MOUTH OPEN to prevent pulmonary and eardrum barotrauma.

2.5. Thermal Infrared Camouflage (FLIR / LWIR)
- The Foil Space Blanket Fallacy: Wrapping foil directly around the body warms the Mylar within 2-3 minutes, creating a blazing beacon on thermal optics.
- Standoff Air Gap Rule: Maintain an insulating air layer of 15-30 cm between your body and the reflective barrier.
- Slanted Overhead Canopies: Pitch tarps at 30-45 degrees to reflect sub-zero sky temperatures (-40 °C).
- Weather Shields: Heavy fog, rain, and snow scatter infrared wavelengths, cutting thermal range by 70-85%.

2.6. Counter-Drone Standoff Netting
- Net Specs: Nylon twine (1.5-2.5 mm) with 25-40 mm mesh size, suspended 1.5-2 meters above trenches or vehicle roofs.
- Effect: Tangling props halts motors without triggering hard fuse horns; premature detonation dissipates in open air.
- L-Shaped Entrances: Entrances must turn 90 degrees; high-speed drones cannot maneuver right-angle turns in tight portals.

================================================================================

SECTION III: ARTILLERY, MORTAR & ROCKET BOMBARDMENT SURVIVAL

3.1. Auditory Signatures of Inbound Shells
- Mortars (82mm & 120mm): Whistling, hissing, fluttering sound. Flight time from sound to blast: 2 to 4 seconds. Dive immediately!
- Tube Artillery (122mm, 152mm, 155mm howitzers): Heavy rising freight-train rumble. Flight time: 8 to 25 seconds.
- MLRS (Grad, Uragan, Smerch): Screaming roar of rocket booster packs; smoke trails visible on horizon. Flight time: 20 to 40 seconds.

3.2. Biological Shockwave Mitigation
- 80% of trauma is caused by shrapnel dispersing in an upward-expanding cone. Prone body posture reduces target surface area by 90%.
- Mechanics: Lie face down, feet toward blast with ankles crossed. Hands over ears, elbows against ribs.
- Open Mouth Rule: Shockwaves spike atmospheric pressure by 1-3 atmospheres. An open mouth equalizes pressure across eustachian tubes, preventing ruptured eardrums and cerebral hemorrhage.
- Slightly arch abdomen off dirt to isolate internal organs from ground shockwaves.

3.3. Structural Shelters: Safe vs Lethal
- Lethal: Glass storefronts (flying glass causes 70% of urban trauma), archways (wind-tunnel effect doubles overpressure), passenger cars, unreinforced cinder blocks.
- Secure: Subways, underground concrete parking, basements of reinforced masonry buildings.
- Two-Exit Rule: Never shelter in a basement with only one entrance; stairwell collapse causes fatal entrapment.

================================================================================

SECTION IV: GRAY ZONE MOVEMENT, RF DISCIPLINE & BLACKOUT

4.1. Urban Movement Tactics
- Avoid open plazas; hug shadowed building plinths.
- 3-Second Bounding Sprints: Exposure time between cover must not exceed 3-4 seconds.
- Prone Corner Clearance: Inspect building corners at ground level or using pocket mirrors.

4.2. Mobile Phones and Electronic Warfare
- Cell phones beacon to IMSI-catchers mimicking cell towers (e.g. Leer-3).
- Clustering of 3-5 active SIM cards triggers automated artillery or glide-bomb strikes.
- Airplane mode is insufficient; use full power-off, battery removal, or Faraday foil pouches (4-5 layers of heavy aluminum foil).

4.3. Blackout Discipline
- Match or lighter flames are visible to Gen-3 NVGs and thermal drones at 1.5-2 km.
- Use only dim tactical RED LIGHT directed straight down onto your feet.

================================================================================
End of manual. KOVCHEG: Offline Autonomous Wartime Safety Compendium.
================================================================================

APPENDICES AND FIELD BALLISTIC ENGINEERING TABLES
Table 1: Standoff Thickness to Stop 7.62x39 / 7.62x54 / 5.56x45 Projectiles:
- Armored Steel Plate: 8-10 mm;
- Dry Sandbags: 40-50 cm;
- Packed Clay Soil: 60-70 cm;
- Solid Brick Masonry: 38 cm;
- Reinforced Concrete: 18-20 cm;
- Solid Pine Timber: 80-100 cm (dry wood is weak ballistic cover!).
